subtopics.title: One String, One Acceleration — the Rules of the System

questions.question: Because the connecting string is inextensible, the two bodies must have:
Because the string is light (massless), the tension is:
options: Larger at the end attached to the heavier body
The same at both ends of the string
Equal to the weight of the string

questions.question: A frictionless, light pulley changes the tension's:
In the two-body system, the tension is classified as:
options: A force acting only on the pulley
An internal force, acting between members of the system

subtopics.title: The Two-Step Method — Whole System, Then One Body

questions.question: The system equation is written first because:
options: It is the only equation in which the unknown tension does not appear
It always gives the tension directly
It avoids using the total mass
The single bodies cannot be analysed at all

questions.question: Trolleys of 6 kg and 4 kg on a frictionless floor are pulled with 40 N. The acceleration is:
For the same trolleys, the tension in the cord to the 4 kg trolley is:
Which is the classic WRONG start for the system equation?
options: Listing only external forces on the pair

subtopics.title: Two Crates on a Rough Floor

questions.question: With μk = 0,15 and total weight 98 N, the total friction on the pair is:
The pair's acceleration under the 40 N pull is:
Analysing the trailing 4 kg crate alone, the friction to use is:
options: Its own 5,88 N, built on its own 39,2 N normal force
Zero, since the cord does the pulling

questions.question: T − 5,88 = 4 × 2,53 gives the cord tension as:

subtopics.title: Over the Pulley — Table Edge and Incline

questions.question: A 3 kg block on a bench (μk = 0,2) is tied over a pulley to a hanging 5 kg mass. The system equation is:
options: 49 − 5,88 = 8a, driving weight minus friction over the total mass

questions.question: That system accelerates at 5,39 m·s⁻². The string tension is:
The tension (22,05 N) is less than the hanging weight (49 N) because:
options: Some tension is lost in the pulley
A net downward force is needed for the mass to accelerate downward
The block absorbs part of the weight

questions.question: On the 30° incline version, the force that opposes the 8 kg hanging driver in the system equation is:
options: The block's weight component along the slope, mg sinθ = 24,5 N

questions.question: Two trolleys tied by a cord move together because:
options: The cord cannot stretch, so they share one acceleration
The front trolley pushes the back one

questions.question: Treating the two trolleys as one long vehicle, the cord's two tugs:
options: Add together to double the force
Act only on the front trolley
Face each other and cancel — the system never feels them

questions.question: A cord or string can exert its force only by:
options: Pushing its object away from the pulley
Pulling, along its own line, toward the partner or pulley
Pushing or pulling, depending on the question

questions.question: Move one of the recipe treats the connected objects as:
options: One object with the combined mass, feeling only outside forces
Two separate objects with separate accelerations
One object with the larger of the two masses
A single object with the cord's tension included

questions.question: For move two, the best body to zoom in on is:
options: Always the body the applied force touches
The laziest one — the body with the fewest forces on it

questions.question: The 10 kg trolley train, pulled with 40 N against 14,7 N of friction, accelerates at:
When zoomed in on the trailing trolley, the friction that belongs in its equation is:
options: Its own friction of 5,88 N and nothing else
No friction — the cord cancels it

questions.question: In the bench-and-dangler setup, the force driving the whole system is:
options: The hanging mass's weight of 49 N

questions.question: The block's own weight and the bench's normal force stay out of the system equation because:
options: They are perpendicular to the block's motion and cancel each other
They are too small to matter

questions.question: While the 5 kg dangler accelerates downward, the string tension is:
options: 22,05 N — less than the hanging weight

questions.question: The string carries the hanging mass's FULL weight only when:
options: Nothing accelerates — the system is at rest or at constant velocity
The block is heavier than the dangler
